summary: The proposal has the required core sections, two referenced figures including an activity diagram, an appropriately detailed AI statement, and two-week iterations tied to objectives. However, it exceeds the 4–6-page text limit, has only five bibliography entries, omits section-specific AI-use information, includes several forbidden/filler sentence openers, and contains schedule items that are undocumented, vague, or internally misdated. Address the critical bibliography gap and major length, transparency, and schedule issues before submission.

findings.title: Bibliography Below Minimum Publication Count
findings.description: The bibliography contains only five publications ([TP21], [AAM17], [BBE10], [Bog+07], and [NM06]), below the required minimum of 6–8. Add at least one more peer-reviewed publication, preferably several to reach the expected range, and cite it where it supports the proposal.

findings.title: High-Level Objectives Use Numbering Instead of Bullets
findings.description: Section 4 presents the high-level objectives as a numbered list, whereas the guideline requires a bullet list. Convert the four one-line entries to bullets while retaining the corresponding subsections.

findings.title: Proposal Text Exceeds the Length Limit
findings.description: The proposal's substantive text extends beyond the permitted 4–6 text pages: the abstract/introduction/problem/motivation/objectives occupy pages 2–8 before the schedule begins on page 9. Condense the explanatory material or move nonessential detail out of the proposal so the text fits the limit.

findings.title: AI Statement Does Not Identify Used Sections
findings.description: The transparency statement names tools and purposes and confirms review, but it does not identify which proposal sections used those tools. Add an explicit mapping, such as the sections in which Grammarly, DeepL, generative tools, Copilot, or Zotero were used.

locations.section: Transparency in the Use of AI Tools
locations.quote: In  preparing    this  proposal,     I made    use  of  several   AI-based     tools  across   diferent stages  of the  writing   process.

findings.title: Filler Transition at Sentence Start
findings.description: This sentence begins with the filler transition “Additionally.” Replace it with a direct formulation, such as “Supervisors can also provide feedback faster…” without using a transition as the sentence opener.

findings.title: Schedule Includes Documentation Task
findings.description: The final iteration includes “Documentation,” which the schedule rules explicitly exclude. Replace it with a development or evaluation deliverable; if thesis documentation is needed, keep it outside the schedule's iteration work items.

findings.title: Bug-Checking Deliverable Is Not Measurable
findings.description: Several schedule items are not measurable deliverables. In particular, “Review the system and check for bugs” does not specify test scope, acceptance criteria, or a resulting artifact. State what will be tested and what constitutes completion.

findings.title: LLM Evaluation Deliverable Is Underspecified
findings.description: The item “Evaluate different LLM models and providers” is too vague to be measurable: it specifies neither the models/providers, evaluation dataset or tasks, metrics, nor a decision artifact. Define those elements and a concrete output.

locations.quote: •   Evaluate    diferent    LLM    models    and   providers    (Objective     3)

findings.title: Schedule Begins Before Thesis Start Date
findings.description: Iteration 1 is scheduled to begin on 08.06.2026, but the proposal states that the Bachelor thesis starts on 26.06.2026. Align the iteration dates with the official thesis period or explain the discrepancy; otherwise the schedule is not internally consistent.
